why_this_matters: Day 86 sits in Phase 5 (Data Visualization + Storytelling), whose goal is: Turn data into charts that change decisions, in matplotlib, seaborn and plotly. Today's core material - Animation frames over time, Choropleth and scatter geo maps, Sunburst and treemap hierarchies - is the vocabulary the rest of the phase is built on. Learners who skip the concept and jump to copying code usually stall two weeks later; the goal here is that you can explain what you did, not just that it ran.

code.heading: Save Plot as `.gif` animation
code.code:
import plotly.express as px
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import io
import PIL


fig = px.scatter(df, x= "gdpPercap",
            y = "lifeExp",
            size= "pop", color= "continent",
            animation_frame='year', animation_group="country",
            log_x=True, size_max=55, range_x=[100,100000], range_y=[5,100])

# generate images for each step in animation
frames = []
for s, fr in enumerate(fig.frames):
    # set main traces to appropriate traces within plotly frame
    fig.update(data=fr.data)
    # move slider to correct place
    fig.layout.sliders[0].update(active=s)
    # generate image of current state
    frames.append(PIL.Image.open(io.BytesIO(fig.to_image(format="png", scale=3))))

# create animated GIF
frames[0].save(
        "./output/gapminder.gif",
        save_all=True,
        append_images=frames[1:],
        optimize=True,
        duration=500,
        loop=0,
        dither=None  # Turn off dithering
    )

import pandas as pd

import io

fig = px.choropleth(monthly_cases, locations='location', locationmode='country names', color = 'total_cases',
                    title='Total Covid Cases Worldwide (January 2021 -to- April 2023)',
                    range_color=[0, monthly_cases['total_cases'].quantile(0.85)],
                    animation_frame= 'year_month', color_continuous_scale='viridis',
                    labels={'year_month':'Year-Month', 'total_cases':'Total Cases'}
                    )
# increase the size of the map
fig.update_layout(height=600, width=800)

# generate images for each step in animation
frames = []
for s, fr in enumerate(fig.frames):
    # set main traces to appropriate traces within plotly frame
    fig.update(data=fr.data)
    # move slider to correct place
    fig.layout.sliders[0].update(active=s)
    # generate image of current state
    frames.append(PIL.Image.open(io.BytesIO(fig.to_image(format="png", scale=3))))

# create animated GIF
frames[0].save(
        "./output/total_covid_cases_worldwide.gif",
        save_all=True,
        append_images=frames[1:],
        optimize=True,
        duration=500, # milliseconds per frame
        loop=0, # infinite loop
        dither=None  # Turn off dithering
    )

common_mistakes.mistake: Watching the lecture without running the repository notebook.
common_mistakes.why: Recognition is not recall: code that looked obvious fails the moment you type it yourself.
common_mistakes.fix: For every topic today, run the linked notebook cell, then retype it from memory in your own file.

common_mistakes.mistake: Using Animation frames over time on data whose types or shape you have not printed.
common_mistakes.why: Most failures in this topic are input problems (dtype, shape, missing values) rather than logic errors.
common_mistakes.fix: Print type and shape immediately before the operation; keep that habit for all 275 days.

debugging.symptom: The linked notebook cell raises ModuleNotFoundError or ImportError.
debugging.cause: Wrong kernel/environment selected, or the library is not installed in the active environment.
debugging.fix: Print sys.executable in the notebook and install into that environment (Day 4).

debugging.symptom: Your output differs from the recording even though the code looks identical.
debugging.cause: Library version differences, a changed default argument, or unseeded randomness.
debugging.fix: Pin versions (requirements.txt), set a random seed, and compare dtypes and shapes, not just values (Day 5).
